name: Melanotan II

lead: Melanotan II (MT-II) is a synthetic cyclic peptide analogue of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone. It was developed in the 1980s at the University of Arizona as part of efforts to produce a sunless tanning agent, and it was also noticed to affect sexual arousal, which led to the later development of the related compound bremelanotide.

It has never been approved as a medicine in major jurisdictions, yet it is widely sold through gray-market vendors as a injectable or nasal-spray tanning product and is discussed heavily in looksmaxxing communities as a way to darken skin and reduce sunburn risk. Regulators such as the UK MHRA and Australia's TGA have issued warnings against its use, and it should not be confused with the prescription drug afamelanotide.

paras: MT-II is a non-selective agonist at several melanocortin receptors. Activation of MC1R on melanocytes shifts melanin synthesis toward eumelanin and darkens the skin, while activity at MC3R and MC4R in the brain is thought to account for effects on appetite, libido and spontaneous erections. Because it acts systemically rather than only on the skin, its effects are not limited to pigmentation.

Reported adverse effects include nausea, flushing, fatigue and unwanted erections, and there are case reports of priapism and renal infarction. Case reports and small series describe new or changing moles, including atypical naevi and several melanomas in users, although causation has not been established and users often had other risk factors. Products are unregulated, so purity, sterility and actual content are unverified. Evidence is limited to small early trials, case reports and anecdote; there are no long-term safety data.
